questions.help:
ILLNESS AND MEDICATION
 
21 Some drugs that can affect driving
Medicines are used to cure and treat illnesses, but a misuse of these substances can lead under certain circumstances to a high number of road traffic collisions.
Not all drugs negatively affect the abilities needed to drive safely, although it is important to know what affect they may have on the driver. Some drugs are considered safe, such as painkillers; whilst others can cause euphoria, sedation, dizziness, impaired concentration and cognitive ability, passiveness, etc.
(Página 48 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  
   
21 Some drugs that can affect driving  
21.1 Antihistamines
These are drugs used to combat allergies.  
The most dangerous ones to affect driving are the socalled ‘first generation’ type. The risk of an accident under the influence of these drugs is similar to that of driving with a blood alcohol content between 0.5 g/l and 0.8 g/l.
The most modern (third generation) do usually cause drowsiness, but can produce adverse effects when mixed alcohol or other drugs.
Many antihistamines do not require a prescription, so there may be people who take these drugs without knowing their side effects. As always, if in doubt consult the doctor or pharmacist.
(Página 48 del manual 'Learning to drive')

17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
Not only alcohol seriously alters the ability to drive a vehicle.
Some pharmaceuticals and the majority of drugs also affect driving because they cause intoxication, problems with attention and concentration and a decreased reaction ability in drivers. If they are mixed with alcohol, the risk of accident is much greater, as it strengthens many of the side effects of these products, and can even produce totally unpredictable reactions.
(Página 43 del manual 'Learning to drive')

ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS    
 
17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.
One of the effects of drugs is that risk perception decreases and some drugs can cause the driver to have an incorrect perception of time and space. The consumption of drugs will never improve reaction time. For people who take drugs and drive, the probability of having an accident is greater. It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Substances excluded are those used under medical prescription and for therapeutic purposes, provided that the driver is able to manage the vehicle and drive with diligence, precaution and without distractions.

6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision    
6.2 The elderly
Other problems that older drivers may potentially face are:
Visual deterioration. Over 30% of those over 65 have serious deficiencies or severe deterioration in vision. As you get older there is a narrowing of the visual field, making it difficult to measure accurately the movement of other vehicles and especially to detect moving objects that are at the ends of the field of vision.  This problem is compounded when driving at night, since older people can also easily suffer from glare.
(Página 255 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Road traffic collisions                
                 
6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision      
6.2 The elderly  
Other problems that older drivers may potentially face are:
Hearing. Over 25% of those over 65 have significant deterioration in their hearing ability. For older people it takes more time to recognise or distinguish
sounds and trace their origin. This lack of hearing can be very dangerous for driving, as important information is lost concerning what is happening around them.
The consumption of medicines. 20% of those over 65 take about five types of medication a day. There are a large number of drugs that can affect the basic skills needed to drive safely.
In the event of a collision older people are more likely to suffer severe injuries and are less likely to survive, due to the their age.
(Página 255 del manual 'Learning to drive')

21 Some drugs that can affect driving  
21.2 The psychoactive (psychotropic) drugs
The effects of psychiatric drugs on driving are:
Anxiolytics, sedatives and hypnotics
Increased sensitivity to sleepiness.
More difficulty in maintaining concentration.
Increased reaction time.
Reflexes and movements slower.
Difficulty coordinating movements.
Periods of blurred vision and eye fatigue.
A magnification of these effects when combined with alcohol.
(Página 49 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
9 Hard shoulders  
 
On some roadways there is an area that runs parallel to the main carriageway, this is called the ‘hard shoulder.’
The following must travel on the hard shoulder, on the right going with the traffic flow, (unless there is a road or part of it specifically designated for their use:
Vehicles pulled by animals.
Special vehicles with a MAM not exceeding 3,500 kg’.
Cycles.
Vehicles following cyclists.
Mopeds.
Vehicles for people with reduced mobility.
However the hard shoulder must be useable. When the road does not have a hard shoulder or it is not useable or sufficient, for instance it is not wide enough, these users must travel as close as possible to the right edge of the roadway, occupying as little as possible of the roadway.
(Página 168 del manual 'Learning to drive')
